answer: Practically, the chain should attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because knoll only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, cedar is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
